transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose I came because I haven’t quite felt like myself. Even when my children sit with me, or the sun is out on my garden—things that ought to make me feel peaceful—I just feel sort of flat inside. Like the part of me that could be glad, or comforted, has shut off. I don’t know if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About two weeks, I think. It started after… after my husband collapsed, and the paramedics were in our kitchen working on him. Since then I just haven’t quite come back to myself. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Are you still able to enjoy activities or hobbies that you usually find pleasurable?

Not really, no… I mean, I still go and sit by the garden, and my children come round, and I’m grateful, truly. But it’s as if I can see that those things should feel nice, and they just don’t reach me. I feel rather flat inside. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you been having any thoughts of guilt or blaming yourself for what happened to your husband?

I… I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been blaming myself exactly. I keep wondering if I should have done something differently, but I don’t know that that’s guilt, is it? I’m sorry, I’m not explaining it very well.
Are you still able to find pleasure in any activities or things?

I wish I could say yes. I do try… when my children come and sit with me, or when the sun is on the garden, I know those are things that ought to comfort me. But it’s like I’m flat inside, like that part of me that can feel glad has shut off. Is that what you mean?
Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself since your husband collapsed?
I… no, I don’t think so. Not harming myself, no. I’ve felt terribly low and shaken, but I wouldn’t want to worry anyone by saying something I don’t mean. Is that all right—does that answer you?
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or how you've been moving around since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed properly. I suppose I’m slower getting about, but I’m 81, so it’s hard to know what’s just… me being older and what’s this. I haven’t been doing much, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you lost any weight since your husband collapsed?
I haven’t really checked, doctor. My clothes don’t seem terribly different, I don’t think… but I haven’t weighed myself. I suppose I wouldn’t want to say I have if I’m not sure. Is that all right?
Have you been having any thoughts that life is not worth living?

I… I don’t know that I’d put it that way, doctor. I’ve been very upset, of course, and everything feels rather hard just now, but I don’t think I’ve been thinking that life isn’t worth living. I hope that’s the right way to answer.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since your husband collapsed?
I haven’t really kept track, to be honest. I suppose I’m eating a bit differently, but I couldn’t say there’s been a clear change in appetite. I don’t want to overstate it if I’m not sure.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping since your husband collapsed?

I’m not sure, doctor. My sleep hasn’t been very regular, but I couldn’t say exactly if it’s changed in a way that matters. I do wake and lie there sometimes, but… I suppose that can happen at my age too, can’t it? Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you felt like you're moving more slowly than usual since you started feeling this way?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that, doctor. I may be a bit slower getting about, but I’m 81, so it’s hard for me to tell what’s this and what’s just… me. I wouldn’t want to say yes if it isn’t really so.
Do you feel like you're resting or sitting still more often than you used to?
I don’t think so… not especially. I do sit down plenty, but I always have at my age. I haven’t really noticed that I’m resting more than I used to. Is that okay—does that answer what you mean?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy and still find pleasure in now?

I wish I could say yes. My children come and sit with me, and I try to be grateful for that… and I still go look at my garden when the sun is on it. Those things used to warm me, you know? But now I just feel sort of flat inside, like the part of me that could feel glad or comforted has shut off. I’m sorry, is that what you’re asking?
Are there any things that you still enjoy or find pleasure in, no matter how small they might seem?

Not really, doctor… I’m trying to think of something small, because I don’t want to sound ungrateful. My children sitting with me should be a comfort, and the sun on my garden used to make me feel glad. But lately it’s just… flat. Like that part of me that could enjoy it has shut off. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you're moving or reacting more slowly than people around you?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’m slower than other people, not in any way I’ve noticed. I mean, I’m 81, so I’m not exactly quick, but that’s been true for a while. Nobody’s said I’m moving oddly slow or anything. Is that what you meant?
Do you feel like you're doing fewer things than you used to?

Yes… I suppose I am doing fewer things. I don’t really go to the senior center anymore, though I keep telling myself I’ll go back when I feel more settled.

And at home, I’m not managing as much as I should. My daughter’s been helping with meals and errands and keeping track of my calendar. I don’t like admitting that. Mostly I stay in the house now, and I avoid the kitchen unless someone’s with me. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you're resting or sitting still more often than you used to, or do you find yourself pacing or being more active than usual?

I’m not sure I’ve really noticed either one clearly. I do sit more, I suppose, but I’m older, so… I don’t know how much of that is just normal. I’m not pacing around or full of energy, no. Mostly I’m just quieter, I guess.

Is that answering it properly?
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety since your husband collapsed?

Restless… no, I don’t think so. Not fidgety in the way you mean, I don’t believe. I might shift around a bit if I’m nervous, but I haven’t noticed myself pacing or not being able to sit still.

I hope that answers it.
